text: The access seed is the legacy roles.txt and Permissions file of RWB-E1-065, held in the rwb-access repository as a migration resource, written by one versioned per-service Flyway migration (V1065_1__access_seed.sql) and one repeatable rebuild migration (R__access_seed_rebuild.sql) in schema rwb_access, carrying the 54 role rows and their permission rows at matrix version PM-2026.12; the DEV seed carries the same matrix version as the one in force in SIT, in line with legacy BR2 (the same DDL as SIT applied to the access data), and the file is re-read at each build so two versions are never merged.
why: The legacy story names the seed file and the 54 roles but no path, format, version label or row count, and no source states whether the DEV label must equal the SIT label; the story needs a fixed label and a fixed file before the migration can be written, and a rebuild must be provably the same rows.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 steps 8 and 10, 8 BR2, 8 BR6, 11 and 13; FSD P4 A2.4 AC-P4-004-01; TSD P4 T3.1 and T3.2; Template and Rules DP-07 and DP-15
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 and 3; section 7 AC1 and AC2; section 8 BR5 and BR10; section 13 Configuration and reference data and Database and migrations
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access tech lead when RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-P1-E1065-CON are published
impact: A different label or file layout changes the migration and the verifier only; the role codes, the letters, the default-deny behaviour and the messages stay as specified.

text: One synthetic test identity per role is provisioned in the DEV directory as a member of the DEV group named in role.entra_group, with a synthetic key of the legacy SYN- convention that carries the role code and a sequence (for example SYN-ID-RW-CASEOWN-01) and no person name; the platform administrator owns the list, the sign-in path of RWB-P4-E1022-APP resolves the identity to its role rows, and the identity is retired when the role receives its first real user (DL39); no identity is stored in rwb_access.
why: BR6 and DL39 require a test user per role before real users, but the target has no identity table and TSD P4 defines role.entra_group only; leaving the owner and the key format open would stop the story and risk a person name in the seed.

text: The rwb-access database login is named 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' in this story until the platform DB story fixes it, and the DEV-only read-only role keeps the legacy name rwb_sandbox_read with SELECT on role and permission only, no UPDATE, and no SELECT on the local access-entry table.
why: The legacy story names the read-only role and the group but not the service login, and the split into per-service schemas means the single-schema grant cannot be copied; the story must not invent a credential name and must not widen a DEV read grant to the access log.

impact: Placeholder names only; no behaviour depends on the literal login name, and the grant list is a DEV configuration change.

text: POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise takes the caller identity from the session, the capability area, the right, the case reference and the field IDs the screen will show, and answers with the decision code (AC-READ or AC-DENY), the matrix version, the scope result and the access-entry reference; GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions answers the identity's roles, default scope, matrix version and letters per capability area; a missing letter or a missing permission row is refused with MSG-P4-002, never allowed.
why: Architecture v5 names both operations and the TSD appendix names neither, so the request and answer have to be fixed as a default before the build; the legacy access case is a refusal on the case list, which needs the answer shape to be testable.

impact: A different shape changes the controller, the contract fake and every caller's client only; the decision codes, the default-deny rule and the messages stay as specified.

text: The DEV seed keeps the legacy count of 54 roles and the 42 role rows of the TSD P4 RBAC matrix as the subset the technical specification fixes; the remaining 12 are administration and non-human actor roles of role class BANK_USER or NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, and the seed file decides both the count and the list, so the verifier compares the seeded rows with the file and not with the matrix table.
why: The two sources disagree on the number of roles and neither enumerates the difference; the seed must have one count before the migration and the identity check can be written, and the file is the only artefact that lists every role.

impact: If the file holds a different count, the verifier's expected count and the identity count change together; nothing else in the story depends on the number.

text: The letters of the 11 capability areas that T6.1 does not tabulate are taken from the legacy seed file only, and an area with no row and an area with a dash both mean default deny; RW-REFADM holds R in Rules and parameters and CRUD in Reference data (the T6.1 row) and no CASE_RECORD row at all, which is what refuses it the case list with MSG-P4-002.
why: The matrix content for most areas exists in no source table, and the refusal in the legacy access case depends on the absence of a CASE_RECORD row for a reference data administrator; without a stated default the build could allow an area by omission.
